recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up source work is needed for FHIR-13517 in core unless a future PA decision changes PractitionerRole.active semantics.
issue_request: FHIR-13517 was a Published/Persuasive PA change request for STU3 asking that PractitionerRole.active stop using Practitioner.active wording and instead describe whether the practitioner role record is active and may be marked not to be used.
initial_application: The issue appears to have been applied by git commit 78b39f30cdbfa85f6d37f5ec56c46ff002f7bbd3, whose subject lists tracker 13517 and whose PractitionerRole spreadsheet diff changed PractitionerRole.active short, definition, requirements, and comments from practitioner-record wording to practitioner-role-record wording.
additional_context: PractitionerRole is an active resource in source/fhir.ini, and the current authoritative StructureDefinition source contains role-specific short, definition, comment, and requirements text. Later Published issue FHIR-32501 expanded the long definition so it is no longer identical to the short display; that later cleanup is already represented on the combined branch and does not reverse FHIR-13517.
reconciliation: No source change was made because the current PractitionerRole.active source already conveys the FHIR-13517 decision: the active flag applies to the practitioner role record, not to the practitioner resource itself, and the old Practitioner wording remains only on Practitioner.active where it belongs.

related_jiras.note: Published/R5 cleanup expanded the PractitionerRole.active long definition while preserving the role-specific wording established by FHIR-13517; an existing combined-branch reconciliation commit already represents that issue.
